l7r/diagram/hamletgen/homesteads/seats.p.note: The cited page finds "the maps seat every farmhouse before they lay any lane". It makes an exception only for a planned Imperial road, and it lays the track out only "once the last house stands". The code does the opposite: it offers seats along lanes already laid, and with connector=True it offers seats along the track out (lines 31-44). The claim admits this is a departure, but it cites the page as if the code followed it. The page does not record this departure; its only recorded DEVIATIONS are the village-scale path-finding and the field-edge facing. The claim's other support, 0033, is not in the bundle. Either the claim should be DEVIATION backed by a drawing-page entry that records this departure, or the code should seat houses before lanes (feature 417 T32).

l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/serve.py::_la.note: §7 says a lane or stretch "that serves nothing is not drawn" and lists "house, field, well, shrine, ford or other way". The code differs in two ways. First, `_trim_to_service(run, segs, houses, steadings=...)` (no `ground`) uses `end_serves`, which counts only a way, a house or a steading: a field's bund, a well, a shrine or a ford does not count. Second, the `len(run) < 2` guard runs before the trim, so a run trimmed to one point (`out[:1]`) goes on to the far-gap branch and can draw its healing link (`_draw_web(s, link[0], ...)`) to a point that serves nothing. The fix: refuse the run when the trim leaves fewer than 2 points, and count the §7 targets

l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/tree.py::lane.note: the claim cites 0081 as what the code implements, but by its own account the code departs from it. The page says a lane that "wanders over another way at such an angle" is cut "where it comes alongside". `off_the_needle` walks back only from the lane's end (`at = mine.length` ... `if at <= 0.0 or at >= mine.length: continue`), so a needle closed mid-lane is never cut and is left for the law to refuse. Relabelling it DEVIATION would not clear it, because the drawing page records no such departure. Either §25 gains a record of the deferral (held until feature 417 T32) and the claim becomes `DEVIATION research/questions/0081-village-lanes.drawing.html`, or the code cuts a mid-lane needle where it comes alongside; a known drift accepted by the round arbiter (ask:417-T45-midlane-needle) to land as filed

l7r/diagram/interactive/place.py::KINDS#.note: 0001 answers this, and the other way: a provincial city's "about 3,000 ... counts only those living within the walls". Either 0001 records the GM's feature-156 ruling, or the claim cites 0001 and the text in place.json follows it. I could not see place.json's wording
the hamlet has no cremation ground or burial ground of its own, and its dead are burned and buried at the main village's

Two parts of the tier text contradict the question. (1) The city's population_note says the figure "does take in the samurai country estates around the city", but the question says it "counts only those living within the walls" and that an estate "stands apart" (§17, §16). (2) The village's "what" says "its tax-free plots", but the question gives one: "one plot of tax-free land" (§5, §7). The other parts match: hamlets per domain 1296/216/40% (§8), no headman and no shrine for a hamlet (§5), the town's 1200 people and 238 households with about two in three farming (§11, §12), not counting the villages (§13), and samurai first appearing at town level (§15). The text should say walls-only and one plot, or the claim should cite a DEVIATION.
